title: Rumor reliability, behavioral impact and source dependence must be separated
problem: Owner asked how R33's ideal warning model handles rumors or leaks.
failure: Treating a rumor as a perfect warning can remove mandatory reserve unsafely; treating repeated copies as independent evidence can inflate confidence from one half to 256/257 in the modeled example.
correction: Separate robust zero-shortfall from expected-loss decisions, trace copies to their source, and use posterior risk only under explicitly allowed risk criteria. A false claim may affect behavior, but this causal mechanism is a separate untested hypothesis in R34.
transfer: Assess source lineage, timing, correctness and actual decision impact separately. Compare an early imperfect signal to a decision-deadline baseline. Do not infer truth from public response or treat rumor labels as calibrated probabilities.
limits: Exogenous binary event, known model probabilities, binary preparation, fixed costs, zero signal cost. 14641 exact finite decision cases and duplicate-signal example. No actual rumor calibration, financial recommendation, causal behavior experiment, originality or independent validation claim.
author: TOTO
